newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC seeks better share valuation - Ospel.
newsitem.headline: SBC seeks better share valuation - Ospel.

text.p: Measures announced with a major restructuring by Swiss Bank Corp, the third-largest bank in Switzerland, should help to boost its share valuation, its chief executive Marcel Ospel said in a newspaper interview.
Ospel, in an interview published in Saturday's edition of Finanz und Wirtschaft, said the restructuring announced by the bank on Wednesday would make its activities more transparent.
This should improve its stock market valuation.
"The desire for transparency is understandable based on the wish for a fair valuation through the stock exchange -- we are under the impression we are undervalued," Ospel said.
Elsewhere in the interview Ospel said the only "effective protection against an 'aggressor' is a high, (or) at least a fair valuation."
Ospel said SBC's retail business was already profitable but corporate lending was not yet profitable.
He expected both areas to improve, with the corporate side likely to begin to be brought into profitability within two to three years.
SBC's restructuring calls for reduction of 1,700 jobs, or 13 percent of SBC's domestic workforce over three years, and closure of 80 retail branch banks out of an existing 325.

SBC will also switch to a new loan-loss provisioning method in which it will initially take a recurring charge of about 600 million Swiss francs in its annual consolidated income statement. In addition, it is setting aside a one-time cushion of 2.0 billion Swiss against unexpected credit loss, plus 400 million francs to cover risks involved in repositioning its corporate client business.
Ospel, asked if he were worried about losing corporate customers, said changes would be ushered in gently.
"We will make it clear to certain clients that they cost us more than they pay us, and invite them to make a broader use of our products," Ospel said.
He added the 400 million franc set-aside indicated certain repercussions could not be ruled out.
SBC will also eliminate major lending risks, or seek to finance them at commensurately higher rates, he said.
SBC feels no pressure to merge with another bank, either inside or outside of Switzerland, Ospel said.

He said SBC would seek to increase business in neighboring areas outside of Switzerland, such as southern Germany, but also said such plans did not call for establishing a physical presence there. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
